note: Top of each column is the AE SPICED deal-review checklist — what you must be able to answer coming out of the call. 'Ask it live' is how to raise it in the room. Don't read the checklist questions aloud; they're written for deal review, not for a prospect.

stages.objective: Establish context and buyer persona map.
dealReview: What's the company, stakeholder, and use case?
Who is the main contact and their role?
What are the company's 3 biggest priorities?
What is their interest in Grace Hill?
askItLive: How many properties do you manage, and what are your top priorities this year?
What are you tracking today, and how connected is it?

stages.objective: Uncover urgency and depth of need.
dealReview: What happens if they do nothing?
askItLive: When performance dips at a property, how do you decide what to fix first?

stages.objective: Quantify and align to strategic goals.
dealReview: Why does the business care now?
askItLive: What would it mean if every property performed like your best one?

stages.objective: Validate urgency and align motion to timeline.
askItLive: What's happening this year that makes this urgent now rather than next budget cycle?

stages.objective: Control the process and ensure clarity.
dealReview: What are the written next steps?
askItLive: Who else needs to be part of this, and what does your approval path look like?

fitIndicators: Relies on individual judgment over a shared standard
Already runs a PMS with adjacent free functionality — so the value case has to clear a real bar

stage2Exit.title: Stage 2 exit — the SQO bar
stage2Exit.note: All seven have to be true before the opportunity advances to Stage 3. The two most commonly skipped are Critical Event (general interest is not a trigger) and a signed-off Mutual Action Plan with a dated next step. Those are also the two that most often turn into a no-decision later.

criteria.detail: Rational and emotional. In their words, with a number attached where possible.
A real deadline or trigger — not just general interest.
Who decides, who signs, what the approval path looks like.
What else is on the shortlist, and which of the four approaches it belongs to.
Decision Maker engaged or a confirmed route to them.
Enough to scope the walkthrough. Custom demo delivered or scheduled.
Dated next step agreed in writing, with owners on both sides.

nextSteps.detail: Pain and impact, in their words.
Technical discovery, success criteria, and a walkthrough built on your properties.
A value case in your numbers, plus commercial terms.
Procurement, contracting, and a kickoff plan.
